name: Mobile App Development
tagline: Build fast, beautiful apps for Android and iOS — natively or cross-platform.

overview.summary: Mobile developers build the apps people use every day on Android and iOS — banking, ride-sharing, food delivery, health, education and games. You can specialise natively (Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS) or use cross-platform frameworks like Flutter and React Native to ship to both platforms from one codebase. Modern mobile work increasingly includes on-device AI, offline-first design, payments and accessibility.
whyTrending: Smartphones are the main — often only — internet device for billions of people, including most users in Bangladesh, so businesses build 'mobile-first'.

Cross-platform tools matured: Flutter and React Native (with its New Architecture) power major production apps, and Compose Multiplatform for iOS reached stable in 2025, letting small teams target both platforms.
On-device AI (Apple Intelligence, Gemini Nano on Android, Core ML, LiteRT) opens a new wave of smart features that need mobile engineers who understand ML integration.
In Bangladesh, MFS apps (bKash, Nagad), ride-sharing, e-commerce and banking apps keep mobile developers in steady demand, and Paylab lists iOS developers among the better-paid IT roles.

beginner: One language: Kotlin, Swift, Dart or TypeScript
Layouts and UI components (Compose, SwiftUI, Flutter widgets)
Calling REST APIs and parsing JSON
Running apps on emulators and real devices
intermediate: Local storage and offline support (Room, Core Data/SwiftData, SQLite)
Publishing to Google Play and the App Store
advanced: Performance profiling: startup time, memory, jank
CI/CD for mobile (Fastlane, GitHub Actions, Codemagic)
On-device ML integration (Core ML, LiteRT/TensorFlow Lite, ML Kit)
Mobile security: certificate pinning, obfuscation, secure payments

stack.note: Native Kotlin/Swift roles pay well at product companies; Flutter is especially popular in Bangladesh and South Asia for agency and startup work.

interview.question: Native vs cross-platform — how do you choose?
interview.answer: Native gives the best performance and earliest access to platform APIs; cross-platform (Flutter/React Native) saves time with one codebase. Choose by team skills, performance needs, budget and platform-specific features.

interview.question: Explain the Android activity lifecycle (or iOS app lifecycle).
interview.answer: Android activities move through onCreate, onStart, onResume, onPause, onStop and onDestroy; you save state and release resources at the right points. iOS has similar scene states: active, inactive, background, suspended.

interview.question: What is MVVM?
interview.answer: Model–View–ViewModel separates UI (View) from presentation logic (ViewModel) and data (Model). The View observes ViewModel state, making code testable and lifecycle-safe.

interview.question: How do you make an app work offline?
interview.answer: Store data locally (Room/SQLite/SwiftData), show cached data first, queue user actions, and sync with the server when connectivity returns, resolving conflicts.

interview.question: How do you avoid a frozen UI?
interview.answer: Never do heavy work on the main thread — use coroutines, async/await, isolates or background threads for network, disk and computation.

interview.question: What is state management in Flutter/React Native?
interview.answer: How app data that affects the UI is stored and updated. Small apps can use local state; larger apps use Riverpod/Bloc (Flutter) or Redux/Zustand/React Query (RN) for predictable updates.

interview.question: How do push notifications work?
interview.answer: The app registers with FCM (Android) or APNs (iOS) to get a device token, your server sends messages to that service, and it delivers them to the device.

interview.question: How do you store sensitive data securely?
interview.answer: Use Android Keystore / EncryptedSharedPreferences or iOS Keychain, never hard-code secrets, and use HTTPS with proper certificate validation.

interview.question: How would you reduce app startup time?
interview.answer: Profile it, defer non-essential initialisation, lazy-load modules, reduce work in the first screen, and use baseline profiles (Android) or optimise launch tasks (iOS).

interview.question: How do you test mobile apps?
interview.answer: Unit tests for logic, UI tests (Espresso/Compose tests, XCTest, Flutter integration tests or Maestro), and testing on a range of real devices and OS versions.

demandNotes.bangladesh: High. Fintech/MFS, e-commerce, ride-sharing and agencies hire mobile developers; Flutter roles are especially common in local postings.
demandNotes.remote: Good demand, especially for Flutter and React Native freelancers who can deliver both platforms; native iOS/Android specialists earn more.
demandNotes.global: High and stable. Mobile remains the primary channel for consumer products worldwide.
